ops.title: When ccx ship reports a rebase conflict on a shared copy, rebase only your commit surgically; then pin new worktrees to origin/main explicitly
ops.body:
When `ccx vcs ship` fails with "rebase onto main conflicts in N commit(s); rolled back" on the shared cc-transcript working copy, the conflict is usually NOT your commit: ship's branch-wide rebase (`-b @-`) drags along sibling commits from concurrent sessions — including pre-existing conflicted leftovers (marked `×` in jj log, containing `.jjconflict-base-0/` trees). Your path-scoped commit did form (the capt-hook "Commit landed" hook fires).

**Why:** Shared jj working copies accumulate other sessions' commits and conflicted debris; only your own commit needs to reach main.

**How to apply:** Recover surgically — never run ship's suggested branch-wide command:
1. `jj log` to find your commit id and confirm it's conflict-free (`if(conflict, ...)` template).
2. `jj rebase -r <your-commit> -d 'bookmarks(exact:"main")'` (single revision, not `-b`).
3. `jj bookmark move exact:main --to <new-id>` then `jj git push --bookmark exact:main`.
4. Verify per [[verify-pushes-against-remote-tree]]: `git diff --stat <old-main>..origin/main` must show ONLY your files.

Side effect: `jj rebase -r` reparents `@` onto your commit's old parent, so the shared working copy loses your files locally and sits on a stale base. Any subsequent worktree for follow-on phases must be created manually pinned to the pushed commit (`git worktree add <path> <sha>`) — workflow `isolation: 'worktree'` snapshots the stale shared-copy HEAD and would miss the just-landed work. Also: a manual push has no CI watch — start a `gh run list --commit <sha>` poller yourself. Related: [[ccx-ship-multi-bookmark-quirk]].
